children: Gold futures lose ground after U.S. consumer price inflation for October comes in above estimates, pushing up yields and firming expectations for a Fed December interest-rate increase. Outflows from ETFs are a headwind for gold, while central bank demand remains a support, Thadeu Dos Santos of Infinox says in a note. "Lower oil prices could provide some offset. Crude has fallen to its lowest level since late August, which may ease inflation pressures and, over time, temper expectations of tighter monetary policy." Gold for December delivery is off 1.4% in New York at $4,058.40 a troy ounce. Silver is down 1.4% at $51.98 a troy ounce. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
